## 107 MALATESTA DI RIMINI AND HIS MISTRESS RECEIVING THE POPE'S LEGATE

Pandolfo Malatesta IV.,Lord of Rimini,notorious for his cruelty and debaucheries; he married Violante, daughter of Giovanni Bentivoglio,of Bologna； during his reign, Rimini was taken by Caesar Borgia in 1499; Pandolfo,however,recovered itin1503,and sold it to the

Venetians

Pandolfo and his mistress are seated near a grove of trees,on stone benches or grave-stones,he with his right hand on her left shoulder;both of them are looking at the Legate, who is standing by,pointing to a skull which he holds in his right hand,and addressing them,probably with the words which are inscribed on a sarcophagus close by"STULTUM EST IN ILLO STATU VIVERE,IN QUO NON AUDET MoRI";the Legate is dressed as a pilgrim, with wallet at his girdle,a shell on his right shoulder,and the cross-keys and papal tiara on his left;in the background is a castle on a hill and other buildings, and beyond again are blue hills
